items.title: kajisho5 / ffmpeg-skill
items.summary: Local video editor for coding agents: 42 FFmpeg tools with a machine-readable contract and an MCP server, for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Cut, captions, reframe, loudness, platform exports. No cloud, no API keys.
items.excerpt: Give your coding agent a video editor. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client edits your footage with local FFmpeg, then checks its own output. No cloud · No API keys · Python standard library Website · Quick start · Demos · Tools · MCP · npm ```bash npx ffmpeg-skill ``` caption.py --animate pop --karaoke fit.py --aspect 9:16 --fit crop silence.py --threshold -35 loudness.py -I -14 --tp -1 Left half is the input, right half is what the command produced. **[Every before/after demo, with the exact command under each one →](docs/demos.md)** — all of it built by `python3 demos/build.py`, so you can rebuild every frame of it yourself. The footage is synthetic (FFmpeg's own test sources) except in three demos, `reframe_talk`, `filler_en` and `pauses_en`, which use two AI-generated clips of people who do not exist ([demos/footage/](demos/footage/README.md)). `ffmpeg-skill` is an [Agent Skill](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/agent-skills) for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and any agent that reads `SKILL.md`. It teaches the agent a fixed workflow (probe → edit losslessly where possible → check → verify) and ships **42 tools** that do the actual work with `ffmpeg` / `ffprobe`: cut, join, silence removal, fit to duration and aspect, captions and karaoke, overlays and motion graphics, HDR → SDR and LUTs, audio clean-up and typed dynamics, sync with drift correction, multicam, loudness, delivery checks, whole-edit project rendering, batch folders. If you build products and hear crickets, this episode gives you workflows you can set up today.
